Article Title: India's bowling lacks bite without Jasprit Bumrah; middle-over planning all over the place
Article Text:
Cardiff [Wales], Jul 16 (ANI): India's Jasprit Bumrah during a warm-up session before the 2nd ODI against England, at Sophia Gardens stadium in Cardiff on Thursday. (ANI Photo)

TimesofIndia.com in London

Poll Vote & Share your view What factor contributed the most to India's loss in the third ODI? Bumrah's absence Poor middle overs bowling Too many extras 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

: Jacob Bethell and Ben Duckett went about a warm, pleasant and sunny morning at the Lord's Cricket Ground on Sunday with some ease. Having won the toss, the duo started slowly but picked up pace as the day went on in the third ODI against India. Arshdeep Singh and Prasidh Krishna took the new ball duties with Jasprit Bumrah unavailable due to an impact injury on his left knee during the second ODI. Reactive swelling on his left knee put India's premier seamer on the sidelines, with Arshdeep taking his spot in the series decider.Krishna plugged the gaps with back-to-back maiden overs as he found his line, length and extra bounce. A streak of 20 dot balls defined the 30-year-old's day out. Unfortunately, with Bumrah not there to aid the effort on the other side, and no one chipping in remotely close to what 'Boom' offers, the struggle to find a wicket or apply pressure by stemming the flow of runs continued.Prince Yadav, coming in as a replacement for the injury-affected Washington Sundar, playing just his third ODI, started by going for 11 runs, including a massive wide that evaded a desperate dive from wicketkeeper Ishan Kishan.If the placid bowling wasn't enough, the extras further played into England's hands. India gifted away 26 extras, including 16 in wides and nine in leg byes."That about sums up India's bowling and day so far," chimed former England captain Nasser Hussain in commentary as Prince Yadav's length delivery on the pads in the 28th over was tickled towards fine leg by Bethell for a boundary. "India will be very disappointed with their bowling today; they've been very ordinary," admitted Ravi Shastri not long after.A 192-run stand between Bethell and Duckett ticked off multiple record boxes. It was England's first century-stand in ODIs since 2023. It was England's biggest stand against India in an ODI. At Lord's, it was the first ton-up stand for the hosts since 2010. It was also the biggest first-wicket partnership at the iconic venue ever.Before Duckett fell to Prince Yadav, scoring 141 off 135 balls, he jotted down milestones of his own. None bigger, possibly, than overhauling Viv Richards' record for the highest score at this venue (138) back in the 1979 World Cup final.England racked up 387/3 on the board -- the biggest ODI score at Lord's since the first-ever World Cup in 1975 -- a day made more famous by Sunil Gavaskar's 174-ball 36 in a 335-run chase.Unlike Gavaskar, Root, another legend of the game, opted for a brisk showing, scoring an unbeaten 48-ball 74. A sixth straight ODI fifty for Root, whom India failed to dismiss even once in the 50-over series. Root amassed 249 runs in three innings and India barely even got close to getting him out.The damage was done by the first-wicket partnership, exacerbated in the middle overs, and the result was all but confirmed in the end. The power play went for 58; the middle overs produced 203/1 and the final 10 overs saw 126 runs, including 62 runs in the last three.Not surprisingly, the bowlers bled runs. Gurnoor Brar conceded 97, Prince another 79, Arshdeep went for 72, and even Prasidh, the pick of the bowlers with two wickets, conceded 69 runs - most of them coming in the slog overs.On a surface that offered support to seamers when there was disciplined bowling, as displayed by Prasidh's dot-ball spell, India were erratic and paid for it. The Men in Blue fielded five frontline bowlers and desperately missed Bumrah while also, once again, deciding to keep Kuldeep Yadav on the bench.The wrist spinner has been involved in just eight ODIs out of the 15 played by the side since India's successful Champions Trophy campaign. His ability to provide breakthroughs in the middle overs has been crucial to India's winning formula. Yet, as India struggle to control the flow of runs and eke out a wicket during that passage, he has not been brought in.The 31-year-old was involved in all three net sessions at Edgbaston ahead of the first ODI and was also busy in the optional session before the series-deciding third. As Sundar picked up an injury, Kuldeep was believed to be the ideal change. Alas, that wasn't to be the case."If you're a side that's able to take wickets through that middle period of the game, it puts you in such a strong position going into the back end of the game. Likewise with the bat, if you're a strong enough side to be able to rotate and pick up boundaries here and there as a batting unit, it sets you up going into the last 10 overs, which can have a massive impact on the game," said England skipper Harry Brook ahead of the third ODI.India, unfortunately for their 2027 ODI World Cup title hopes, haven't challenged consistently in these middle overs. Against New Zealand in three ODIs, the middle overs saw: 163/5, 193/2 and 191/1. That scenario improved against Afghanistan before, once again, looking dire against England: 152/6, 146/4 and 203/1.India's seam bowling effort without Bumrah looked uninspired and insipid. The day out at Lord's appeared more a case of Sunday cricket with the bowlers going about their motion without much of a thought involved. The bulk of the deliveries landed full and were duly dispatched for 105 runs. At the other end of the surface, India seamers bowled 38 short balls and were whacked for 87 runs, going at an economy rate of 13.73. When the bowlers did get their line right, on 77 balls, they let go of 58 runs.Ultimately, the 388-run target proved to be a bridge too far. It was a consequence of more than just one poor outing. Bumrah's absence exposed the lack of bite in the pace attack, but the larger concern, perhaps, remains India's inability to seize control through the middle overs.While England's batters executed their plans with clarity, India were left searching for answers, persisting with combinations that have repeatedly failed to stem the flow of runs. With 15 months to go before the 2027 ODI World Cup, these recurring issues are becoming less about experimentation and more about missed opportunities to settle on a bowling formula that can consistently take wickets, apply pressure and win matches.
Article Summary: Jacob Bethell and Ben Duckett put on 192 for the first-wicket partnership. England racked up 387/3 on the board, the biggest ODI score at Lord's since 1975. Jasprit Bumrah missed the third ODI due to an impact injury on his left knee.

Article Title: Rohit Sharma fires but India fold at Lord's, finish tour with just one win
Article Text:
Rohit Sharma

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think needs to improve for India in the ODI format? Batting consistency Bowling attack Team strategy Captain's decision-making 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

For a team management which has refused to talk up personal milestones, a 39-year-old Rohit Sharma brought out a knock that left every cricket fan thrilled to bits. Chasing an improbable target of 388 in the series decider and striving to extend his career beyond this match, Rohit became the first Indian to score an ODI hundred at Lord's on Sunday.Rohit's knock of 138 off 110 balls is bound to trigger raging debates over his place in India's ODI World Cup plans. But it must not be lost on the caretakers of Indian cricket that India have lost three out of the last four ODI series with India going down by 27 runs on a pitch which was closest to the surfaces in India. Head coach Gautam Gambhir will board the flight from London having won just one match on a white-ball tour which also includes suffering a T20I whitewash at the hands of Ireland. Shubman Gill is yet to win a series since he took over the captaincy from Rohit last October.Discussions around India's preparation for next year's World Cup have largely revolved around Rohit at the top of the order. As he has been doing of late, Rohit fired in the fag end of a series. And as India have been doing of late, their batting is consistently coming second to the oppositions in high-scoring matches. Most importantly, it is well established by now that the bowling attack is invariably out of breath without Jasprit Bumrah, who sat out due to an impact injury suffered in the last ODI in Cardiff.The English batting feasted on the young Indian bowling attack with Ben Duckett scoring 141 off 135 and Jacob Bethell hitting 91 off 93 followed by Joe Root's unbeaten74 off 48 and Jos Buttler's defining unbeaten 13-ball 41.Rohit did what he had to tell the team management and the selectors that he isn't done with playing for India. The innings may not have had the fluency and array of strokes that one associates with Rohit, but it screamed of his resilience and mental strength of a champion. The start offered by Gill and Rohit was bizarre with the duo going at around 5-5.5 runs per over for the first 20 overs of a chase that demanded a run rate close to 7.5 runs per over.Rohit did cut loose once India lost Gill for 77 off 84 balls at the score of 147 and Virat Kohli striding out with an intent to chase down this total. Rohit's struggles against the good length ball on off stump were evident as he waited for the short balls to unleash his vintage pull shots. His first boundaries down the ground came nearly around the 30 over mark once he got absolutely settled. It felt like he was in familiar territory with Kohli in his ears at the other end. The chase really began after 25 overs and it fizzled out with a cramping Rohit falling in the 39th over. With the 103-run partnership in about 14 overs, Kohli and Rohit rolled back time but hopes of a miracle ended as Kohli departed for 74 off 60.
Article Summary: Rohit Sharma becomes first Indian to score an ODI hundred at Lord's. Shubman Gill is yet to win a series since he took over the captaincy from Rohit last October. India have lost three out of the last four ODI series.

Article Title: Nine runs to win, 1 wicket in hand: New Zealand clinch thriller to take unassailable 3-1 lead over West Indies
Article Text:
Mitchell Santner

While much of the sporting world was focused on the FIFA World Cup final in New Jersey, New Zealand and West Indies played out a tense one-day international at Kensington Oval in Bridgetown, where both teams paid tribute to Sir Garry Sobers.New Zealand held their nerve to beat West Indies by one wicket in a low-scoring contest, taking an unassailable 3-1 lead in the five-match ODI series.Captain Mitchell Santner led the chase with an unbeaten 34, guiding the lower order through the closing stages after New Zealand looked in danger of falling short. No. 11 Jayden Lennox also played an important role, surviving 10 deliveries in an unbeaten stand of nine runs with Santner to help the visitors cross the line.Lennox had been named Player of the Match in each of the previous two games for his bowling performances.Earlier, Mark Chapman top-scored for New Zealand with 80 after West Indies were bowled out for 188 on a two-paced surface.With three runs needed and one wicket remaining, Santner was dropped before Lennox survived reviews for both a caught-behind and an lbw appeal. New Zealand eventually reached the target with 35 balls to spare.“It was pretty chaotic, especially the ending,” Santner said. “You try to chip off the total as much as you can. Even partnerships of 10 or 15 at that stage was going a long way.“It probably shouldn't have got that close but it was nice to get over the line.”The match was played two days after the death of Sir Garry Sobers, who died on Friday at the age of 89. Playing in Sobers' hometown of Bridgetown and at Kensington Oval, where he built his career, West Indies had hoped to honour one of the country's greatest cricketers with a victory.Both teams wore black armbands, flags flew at half-mast, two seats in the Sir Garry Sobers Pavilion were left empty, and a minute's silence was observed before the start of play.Sobers is widely regarded as the greatest West Indies cricketer and one of the finest all-rounders in the history of the game, scoring more than 8,000 Test runs and taking over 200 wickets.West Indies' hopes of a fitting tribute suffered an early setback when New Zealand won the toss and chose to bowl. Teams batting second have now won all four matches in the series.The home side slipped to 58 for 3 and then 81 for 6 before Amir Jangoo and Gudakesh Motie added 81 runs for the seventh wicket to revive the innings.Jangoo scored 51 from 71 balls, while Motie contributed 41 to take West Indies to 188.Young fast bowler Matthew Fisher claimed 3 for 40, his first ODI wickets for New Zealand.
Article Summary: New Zealand hold their nerve to beat West Indies by one wicket in a low-scoring contest. Captain Mitchell Santner led the chase with an unbeaten 34, guiding the lower order through the closing stages. The match was played two days after the death of Sir Garry Sobers, who died on Friday at the age of 89.

Article Title: Ryan Fox hunts down history at the Open
Article Text:
Ryan Fox

Royal Birkdale (Southport): There was no dearth of drama at the 154 th Open which literally went to the wire. No less than seven players reached at least eight-under at some point and no one went past 11-under, before the roulette ball got stuck at nine-under for more than two and half hours.Then, first gingerly but surely, it slipped into the 10-under slot as New Zealand’s Ryan Fox holed the final putt from just under 12 feet to get past American Cameron Young’s clubhouse target of nine-under, which was set when Fox had not yet reached the turn in his final round.Son of former All Black rugby union international Grant Fox, the New Zealander found four birdies in his last four holes in a dramatic finish and from almost nowhere at turn, he raced past the post and opposition despite a bogey on the Par-3 15 th . With the crowd holding its breath, Fox held his nerve and putted out from 12 feet to leave Young stranded once again.Fox (68) finished 10-under, as Young (64), who rallied from three-under to nine-under, was second. Overnight leader, Sam Burns (72), who almost did not make it to the Open to be with his newborn daughter, rose to 11-under before lunging and plunging to three straight bogeys from fourth hole to fall to eightunder and stayed there till the end to be third.Defending champion Scottie Scheffler (67) never gave up till the end. He needed an impossible eagle on Par-4 18 th and ended with a bogey for a seven-under and was tied fourth with Southport born Tommy Fleetwood seeing his chances evaporate after three bogeys in a row in the middle of the round from the ninth to the 11th .
Article Summary: New Zealand's Ryan Fox holed the final putt from just under 12 feet to get past American Cameron Young’s clubhouse target of nine-under. Fox (68) finished 10-under, as Young (64), who rallied from three-under to nine- under, was second. Overnight leader, Sam Burns (72), rose to 11-under before lunging and plunging to three straight bogeys from fourth hole to fall to eightunder and stayed there till the end.

Article Title: Argentina's Emiliano Martinez makes history with record-breaking 11 saves in heartbreaking FIFA World Cup final loss against Spain
Article Text:
Argentina goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez (23) saves a shot by Spain's Nico Williams (17) during the World Cup final between Spain and Argentina.(AP/PTI)

The Stoppage-Time Miracle

Argentina may have surrendered their global crown to Spain at MetLife Stadium, but goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez etched his name into footballing record books by producing the single greatest shot-stopping performance ever witnessed in a FIFA World Cup final.Throughout 120 agonizing minutes on Sunday night, the 33-year-old custodian stood as a human wall against a relentless Spanish attack. Martínez racked up an astonishing 11 saves, the most ever recorded by a goalkeeper in a World Cup final since official data tracking began in 1966.With Argentina severely struggling to generate forward momentum—failing to register a single shot in regulation time—Spain took total command of the pitch. La Roja peppered the Argentine penalty area, unleashing continuous long-range drives and sharp box entries. Time and time again, Martínez kept the Albiceleste alive.He parried long-range rockets from Pau Cubarsí and Nico Williams, adjusted brilliantly to tip a deflected Lamine Yamal effort wide, and scrambled across his line to collect point-blank header attempts. As Argentina's outfield defensive block buckled, Martínez repeatedly bailed out his backline with heroic positioning and reflex reactions.The crowning moment of Martínez's record-setting night arrived deep into regulation stoppage time, immediately after midfielder Enzo Fernández received a red card. Faced with a dangerous 22-yard free kick from teenage prodigy Lamine Yamal, the ball curled dangerously toward the top corner. Martínez launched himself across the goal frame, producing an acrobatic fingertip save to push the ball clear and send the match into extra time.Martínez’s 11th and final save kept the scoreline deadlocked until the 106th minute, when substitute Ferran Torres finally managed to slide a strike past him into the roof of the net. While Spain walked away with the 1-0 victory and their second World Cup title, Martínez’s colossal individual performance stands alone as a landmark statistical achievement in international football history.
Article Summary: Emiliano Martínez made 11 saves, the most ever recorded by a goalkeeper in a World Cup final since official data tracking began in 1966. The 33-year-old custodian stood as a human wall against a relentless Spanish attack. Spain walked away with the 1-0 victory and their second World Cup title.

Article Title: Argentina equal Brazil's 24-year-old World Cup record, eye historic perfect title defence against Spain
Article Text:
Argentina's Lionel Messi (10) applauds the crowd during the World Cup. (AP Photo)

One win away from a flawless World Cup



Uruguay (1930) – 4 wins from 4 matches

Italy (1938) – 4 wins from 4 matches

Brazil (1970) – 6 wins from 6 matches

Brazil (2002) – 7 wins from 7 matches

Spain stand in the way of history



Defending champions Argentina stand on the brink of another slice of football history as Lionel Scaloni's side prepare to face Spain in the FIFA World Cup 2026 final, with a chance to set one of the game's rarest achievements while completing a remarkable title defence.The reigning champions have already equalled a 24-year-old World Cup record by becoming only the second team in history to win seven matches at a single edition of the tournament. The only other side to accomplish that feat was Brazil during their triumphant 2002 campaign in Japan and South Korea.Now, one more victory in Sunday's final at the New York New Jersey Stadium would elevate Argentina into an even more exclusive club.Argentina have won all seven of their matches en route to the final, defeating England 2-1 in a dramatic semifinal after coming from behind through goals from Enzo Fernandez and Lautaro Martinez.Victory over Spain would make Lionel Messi and company only the fifth team in World Cup history to win every match on their way to lifting the trophy.Only four champions have previously achieved a perfect campaign:Argentina now have the opportunity to join those legendary teams while becoming the first nation since Brazil in 2002 to complete a flawless World Cup.They will also become first to win eight matches in one edition.Standing between Argentina and history is a confident Spanish side chasing their second World Cup title after their triumph in 2010.Luis de la Fuente's team has impressed throughout the tournament, conceding just one goal in seven matches while recording six clean sheets. Spain booked their place in the final with a composed 2-0 victory over France, thanks to goals from Mikel Oyarzabal and Pedro Porro.Ahead of the title clash, De la Fuente predicted an entertaining contest between two teams committed to attacking football."There are two top-class sides, two superb teams with many similarities... I think it's going to be a cracking match," the Spain coach said.Argentina boss Lionel Scaloni, meanwhile, insisted his side must produce its best performance despite their perfect run."We need to bring out our best version to try to win. We're a team that's already well-known by our rivals, and that's why it has double merit to have reached where we have. We'll try to win the final," Scaloni said.The Argentine coach also hailed Messi's extraordinary journey to another World Cup final at the age of 39."Having been able to reach a final the way Leo has... is incredible. We have to value what he does and the story and the legend that he is," Scaloni added.Sunday's final therefore offers far more than a battle for the trophy. For Argentina, it is an opportunity to equal Brazil's perfect 2002 campaign, complete back-to-back World Cup triumphs, and cement this generation's place among the greatest teams the sport has ever produced.
Article Summary: Defending champions Argentina face Spain in the FIFA World Cup 2026 final. Lionel Scaloni's side have won all seven of their matches on their way to the final. Victory over Spain would make them only the fifth team in World Cup history to win every match on the way to lifting the trophy. Only four champions have previously achieved a perfect campaign.

Article Title: Spain forced to abandon 'most important' World Cup final training ahead of showdown with Argentina due to thunderstorms
Article Text:
A New York Red Bulls logo is displayed on a glass window at the MLS soccer team's former training facility in Whippany, N.J., Saturday, July 18, 2026, before Spain's training session ahead of Sunday's World Cup final against Argentina (AP Photo/Julio Cortez)

Spain forced to cancel session after delays

De la Fuente had stressed importance of final session

Argentina train despite difficult conditions

Wildfire smoke concerns and improving air quality

Conditions expected to improve for final

Just one day before the 2026 FIFA World Cup final, both Spain and Argentina saw their preparations disrupted by severe weather after thunderstorms sweeping across northern New Jersey forced changes to their final scheduled training sessions.The two finalists are due to meet on Sunday at the New York New Jersey Stadium, but instead of completing their final tactical work on the pitch, both camps found themselves dealing with delays caused by lightning, torrential rain and strict FIFA safety protocols.Spain were the worst affected. Luis de la Fuente's side arrived on schedule for their final session at the former New York Red Bulls training base on Melanie Lane in Whippany, with training originally set to begin at 11 a.m. local time. However, a FIFA official informed reporters that training could not commence unless there had been at least 30 consecutive minutes without lightning within an eight-mile radius of the facility, as required under tournament protocol.With storms continuing to pass through the area and no safe window emerging, Spain waited for around 40 minutes before abandoning the outdoor session altogether.Reporter Guillem Balague, who was at the training base, shared footage showing torrential rain and flooded roads around the facility as thunderstorms swept across New Jersey.Rather than continue waiting inside the dressing rooms, De la Fuente and his coaching staff opted to cancel the outdoor session completely, with the squad instead carrying out an extended gym workout indoors.The cancellation came just 24 hours after the Spain manager described the final training session as one of the most important of the tournament, particularly with Lamine Yamal and Pedro Porro managing minor knocks following the semifinal victory over France."Tomorrow we have the last training session. It's one of the most critical moments, thinking that there can't be any delays because you won't make the game if there were some sort of adverse circumstance – hopefully not," De la Fuente had said on Friday before adding reassuringly: "But they're all good."Argentina's preparations were also interrupted by the same weather system.Lionel Scaloni's squad, scheduled to train around five miles away at the Red Bulls Performance Center in Morristown, initially delayed their session after lightning strikes were detected in the area. Their practice was pushed back by roughly 45 minutes before the defending champions eventually emerged onto the rain-soaked pitch to complete training despite the difficult conditions.The thunderstorms marked the latest weather-related challenge to affect the tournament. Throughout the week, concerns had centred on Canadian wildfire smoke drifting across the northeastern United States, prompting New York City emergency officials to issue a Code Red air quality alert between Tuesday and Thursday. Residents were advised to remain indoors where possible and avoid strenuous outdoor activity as smoke spread across much of the region.Saturday's storm, however, is expected to bring one important benefit.Meteorologists believe the rainfall will help clear much of the lingering haze before Sunday's final. The Air Quality Index, which reached approximately 160 on Saturday and was classified as "unhealthy", is forecast to improve to around 100, a "moderate" level, by kickoff.While the disrupted preparations were far from ideal for either finalist, organisers remain confident that weather conditions will improve in time for Sunday, allowing Spain and Argentina to contest the World Cup final under significantly healthier conditions than had been feared earlier in the week.
Article Summary: Spain and Argentina's final training session disrupted by severe weather. Thunderstorms sweeping across northern New Jersey forced changes to their final scheduled training sessions. Luis de la Fuente's side forced to cancel session after delays caused by lightning, torrential rain and strict FIFA safety protocols. Argentina's practice was pushed back by roughly 45 minutes.

Article Title: FIFA WC 2026: Thunderstorms will clear wildfire smoke from New York haze ahead of World Cup final
Article Text:
The Statue of Liberty stands during sunset as smoke from wildfires blankets the sky, in the Brooklyn borough of New York. (AP/PTI)

In a major relief for football fans and organizers, severe thunderstorms passing through the Northeast United States are expected to clear the toxic Canadian wildfire smoke just in time for Sunday's mega World Cup final between Spain and Argentina at MetLife Stadium.Thick, gray smog had enveloped the region for days, triggering severe air quality warnings. On Saturday, heavy rain, booming thunder, and lightning lashed the open-air stadium, forcing state police to evacuate the seating bowl and field for shelter. The extreme weather even forced the Spanish national team to suspend their final pre-match training session due to safety concerns. FIFA officials confirmed they are monitoring the field conditions every ten minutes.However, meteorologists have brought good news, stating that the aggressive storm front will successfully "sweep the atmosphere clean" before the final kickoff. The air quality index in East Rutherford is predicted to improve from "unhealthy" on Saturday to a safe "moderate" level on Sunday."It won't be dangerous anymore. It's going to be dramatically better," said climate specialist Jeff Berardelli, adding that conditions for the match will be nearly perfect, with temperatures hovering around a pleasant 27 degrees Celsius, accompanied by low humidity and a light breeze.While the weather is clearing, a political storm has ignited over the environmental crisis. US President Donald Trump heavily criticized Canada on social media, accusing the neighbor of invading the US with "filthy, polluted, and unhealthy air" and threatening to impose new trade tariffs in retaliation.Canadian leaders hit back quickly. Ontario Premier Doug Ford called the tariff threats "absolutely unacceptable and shortsighted," pointing out that Canadian firefighters frequently help the US during natural disasters. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney also weighed in, stating that global climate change is a shared responsibility. Currently, hundreds of unprecedented, lightning-triggered wildfires continue to burn across Canada, forced evacuations and scorching record amounts of land.
Article Summary: Thick, gray smog had enveloped the region for days, triggering severe air quality warnings. On Saturday, heavy rain, booming thunder, and lightning lashed the open-air stadium. The extreme weather even forced the Spanish national team to suspend their final pre-match training session due to safety concerns.

Article Title: 'Gave away a lot of runs': Shubman Gill rues costly death overs as England beat India by 27 runs to seal ODI series
Article Text:
Shubman Gill and Gurnoor Brar during 3rd ODI against England, at Lord's in London on Sunday. (ANI Photo)

India captain Shubman Gill said his side lost control of the match after conceding too many runs in the final overs of England's innings, as the hosts secured a 27-run victory in the series-deciding third ODI on Sunday.England posted 388 after a late flourish with the bat, a total that Gill felt proved beyond India's reach despite the visitors remaining in the contest for most of the innings."We were right in the game until the 45th over (when England batted). Gave away a lot of runs in the last three overs. That's where the game went away from us," Gill said at the post-match presentation ceremony.Explaining India's chase, Gill said the plan was to preserve wickets before accelerating in the closing overs."We thought if we had wickets in hand after 40 overs, we would be in the game. At the same time, we didn't want to be too far behind. After the powerplay we tried to play at 6-6.5 runs per over and chase at 10 in the last 10 overs," he said.Gill also praised Rohit Sharma for his century, saying the veteran opener showed his class on a pitch that became increasingly difficult for batting."They (Rohit and Kohli) have done well over the years in different parts of the world.Pleased with how Rohit batted today. The wicket got slow in the end, wasn't easy to bat, but treat to watch."India struggled with the ball throughout the innings, particularly in the powerplay and at the death, allowing England to build on contributions from Ben Duckett, Jacob Bethell and Joe Root before finishing strongly."Almost everyone got runs. In this match particularly, we didn't bowl well in the first powerplay. The way they capitalised never gave us chance to come back. At the death, they got too far away from us," Gill said.England captain Harry Brook praised his team's response after losing the opening ODI, saying the series win over the world's top-ranked side reflected the team's resilience and execution."Extremely proud. Fought hard, communicated well and manage to escape away with a series win over the world No. 1. Spoken about setting a template. Duckett and Bethell were sensational. Outstanding partnership. Rooty doing what Root does. Jos finishing the innings was awesome to watch."Brook also credited head coach Brendon McCullum for encouraging him to persist with Jacob Bethell during a crucial spell."I went off for an over and had a chat to Baz. He said why don't you have a crack with Beth, and bowl him for seven or eight overs straight through. It was tough at times but we got the job done," Brook said.

Article Title: Rohit Sharma's historic ton goes in vain as India lose ODI series at Lord's
Article Text:
Rohit Sharma

With his back against the wall and an illustrious career on the line, Rohit Sharma silenced his critics the only way he can, smashing one of his most celebrated centuries in recent memory, though it wasn't enough to prevent a 27-run defeat in the third ODI against England, as India surrendered the series 1-2 at Lord's on Sunday.Despite Rohit's magnificent 138, Shubman Gill's 77 and Virat Kohli's 74, India only managed 360 for 7 in pursuit of a mammoth target of 388 built on the back of a career-best 142 from Ben Duckett and 91 from Jacob Bethell.The 13-ball 41 from Jos Buttler proved to be the decisive factor as England scored 82 in their last five overs.With speculations about selectors and the head coach ready to move on from Rohit going forward, the 39-year-old former skipper faced enormous pressure going into the third and final game.Rohit walked onto the hallowed turf of Lord's with a dual target: winning a series for India and saving his legacy, which was being tarnished by constant speculation from a section of the media.He didn't raise his bat after completing his 34th ODI hundred -- the first by an Indian batter at Lord's. Nor did he acknowledge the standing ovation from the suits at the Members' Balcony after a 110-ball knock stitched with heart, hurt, and sweat.It was the last time he played an ODI in England, and people would talk for the longest time about how an ageing star showed resolve when the powers that be made him feel unwanted.A stand of 147 with skipper Gill and 113 with his old pal Kohli raised visions of an improbable victory.For Rohit, there were 17 boundaries and five sixes -- three off Josh Tongue -- a pull, one down the ground, and one wide off long-on. There was a pulled six off Sam Curran (4/75 in 10 overs), who proved to be the bowling hero for England.Curran's pace off deliveries at the death accounted for Ishan Kishan, Shreyas Iyer and Kohli in a space of seven deliveries to end any hopes that India would have harboured.Curran got able support from left-arm spinner Jacob Bethell (1/49 in 7 overs), a luxury India never had by playing a lone spinner in Axar Patel.While India lost the series, one thing is for sure: neither Rohit nor Kohli will be going anywhere until the 2027 World Cup in South Africa.On the day, Gambhir and Gill's planning went haywire and playing four pacers with combined experience of 51 games backfired badly.Jasprit Bumrah's absence due to an impact injury on his left knee was a blow for India.The four-pronged pace attack comprising Prasidh Krishna (2/69 in 10 overs), Arshdeep Singh (0/72 in 10 overs), Prince Yadav (1/79 on 10 overs) and Gurnoor Brar (0/97 in 10 overs), lacked both skill and experience against an in-form batting line-up.Duckett and Bethell were fantastic in terms of planning and execution. The batting powerplay of first 10 overs yielded 58 runs but the wheels came off between overs 11 to 30 when they literally ran the bowlers ragged.With head coach Gambhir using Kuldeep Yadav in only 38 games out of a total 103 matches (across three formats) since his appointment in 2024, the lack of a second spinner save Axar Patel (0/61 in 10 overs) did hurt India.While Duckett hit 18 boundaries in all apart from a six, Bethell, who looked comparatively more fluent at the onset, hit 11 fours and a six, before being holed out in the deep off Prasidh Krishna's bowling.Joe Root (74 no off 48 balls) continued his golden run of form with another half-century -- his third in three games -- to take the total past 350-run mark. Jos Buttler (41 no off 13 balls) also joined in the fun as Brar got a harsh lesson in international cricket, going for almost 100 runs.At the onset, it didn't help matters that rookie Prince, bowling up the famous Lord's slope, struggled with his length as Bethell pulled him for a six over deep mid-wicket and then slapped him in the gap between deep mid-wicket and mid-on for a boundary.The rusty Arshdeep Singh didn't hold his line while Prasidh Krishna, despite beating Bethell's bat on a number of occasions, also bowled the odd loose delivery.However, Bethell did well to complete his half-century off 51 balls while England reached the team total of 100 by the 16th over. By that time, Indian bowlers have already conceded 15 boundaries and the lines were horribly wrong, allowing the opening pair to nicely settle into a rhythm. In all, they conceded 42 boundaries and six sixes.It also established the fact that all the other Indian pacers look good when the brilliant Bumrah is at work at one end and that effectiveness vanishes once he is absent. One saw that in the T20Is and now in ODIs too.
Article Summary: India lose third ODI by 27 runs at Lord's to lose series 1-2. Rohit Sharma scores 138, Shubman Gill 77 and Virat Kohli 74. Ben Duckett and Jacob Bethell hit career-best scores of 142 and 91 respectively.

Rohit Sharma added another milestone to his remarkable ODI career during the series-deciding third ODI against England at Lord's, overtaking Virat Kohli for the most 50-plus scores by a visiting batter in England.The former Indian captain brought up his 15th ODI score of 50 or more on English soil, moving past Kohli's tally of 14. The partnerships kept India firmly in the hunt despite the stiff target.Rohit's superb knock eventually ended in the 39th over when left-arm spinner Jacob Bethell bowled him with a delivery that beat his attempted sweep and crashed into middle stump.As the opener walked back, Lord's rose to applaud the innings, while Kohli patted him on the helmet in appreciation.By the time he departed, India had raced to 260/2, with Kohli unbeaten at the crease and the chase well within reach. Rohit Sharma etched his name into cricket's record books on Sunday by becoming the batter with the most ODI centuries in a visiting country, producing a magnificent hundred at Lord's that helped India stay alive in the series-deciding third ODI against England.The landmark knock was Rohit's eighth ODI century in England, taking him past Indian legend Sachin Tendulkar and placing him alone at the top of an elite all-time list.The century was another remarkable addition to Rohit's glittering ODI legacy. Among all batters in England, only Joe Root (10) has scored more ODI hundreds in the country, while former England opener Marcus Trescothick also has eight.Coming under intense scrutiny after failing to register a fifty-plus score in his previous eight ODI innings and amid speculation over his future, the 39-year-old responded in the most emphatic fashion with his 34th ODI century at the Home of Cricket.The innings also saw Rohit rewrite several records at the iconic venue.At 39 years and 80 days, he became the oldest batter to score an ODI century at Lord's and also the oldest Indian to score an international century across all formats.More significantly, Rohit became the first Indian batter to score an ODI hundred at Lord's, surpassing Sourav Ganguly's 90 against England in 2004, which had stood as India's highest individual ODI score at the venue for over two decades.The milestone came in trademark Rohit style. Facing Adil Rashid in the 31st over, the Indian opener swept a flighted delivery over cow corner for four to bring up his century. As the ball raced to the boundary, the entire Indian dressing room, including head coach Gautam Gambhir, rose in applause. Rohit acknowledged the standing ovation from the packed Lord's crowd before receiving a warm embrace from Virat Kohli.It was a measured innings that began cautiously before blossoming into vintage Rohit strokeplay, silencing critics who had questioned his place after a prolonged lean run.Earlier, England had posted a daunting 387/3, the highest ODI total ever recorded at Lord's.Ben Duckett starred with a brilliant 141 to become only the sixth batter to score both Test and ODI centuries at Lord's, while Jacob Bethell struck 91 during a 192-run opening partnership.Joe Root continued his extraordinary consistency, extending his unbeaten streak in the series to 249 runs while becoming the first England batter to register six successive ODI fifty-plus scores. Jos Buttler then smashed an unbeaten 41 off just 13 deliveries as England plundered 63 runs in the final 19 balls.The late blitz also produced the fastest 50-plus partnership against India in ODI history, with Root and Buttler scoring at a run rate of 19.89.

NEW DELHI: The first-ever halftime show in a FIFA World Cup final failed to impress former England captain Wayne Rooney . The match between Spain and Argentina at the New York New Jersey Stadium featured an extended halftime break, with FIFA increasing the interval from the usual 15 minutes to more than 27 minutes for an 11-minute entertainment show.Artists including Madonna, Shakira Justin Bieber , Burna Boy and BTS performed, while Hollywood star Tom Cruise, Robbie Williams, Jennifer Hudson, Nicole Scherzinger, Laura Pausini, Post Malone, Swae Lee and streamer IShowSpeed also appeared as part of the closing ceremony.But Rooney was far from impressed.Working as a BBC pundit alongside Joe Hart and Micah Richards, Rooney gave a blunt review when asked about his favourite moment from the show."I'll be honest, mine was when it finished. I like Burna Boy, I like Bieber, I like Shakira, but that was too flat."After the long halftime break, Spain finally found the breakthrough in extra time to beat defending champions Argentina 1-0 and lift their second FIFA World Cup title.Substitute Ferran Torres scored the winner in the 106th minute after a move involving Lamine Yamal, Pedro Porro and Nico Williams.Torres dedicated the goal to the people of Spain.“I think at the end of the day, it was a goal scored by 47 million people,” Torres said.“I feel very happy. I was heavily criticized during the World Cup, but I think it was written in destiny and things. But I always have that chance, that option to continue, and God gives it to those who believe it, who deserve it most,” he said.

The post was made before Argentina won the 2022 World Cup in Qatar and even before Spain wonderkid Lamine Yamal had made his senior debut for Barcelona.The prediction resurfaced on the morning of the final, attracting millions of views and becoming one of the biggest talking points on social media.Believing the remarkable forecast could come true, McGregor backed the exact scoreline."What's up folks, Conor McGregor here with my World Cup final bet," he said in a video posted to Instagram."The bet will be Argentina to beat Spain 3-2 within the 90 minutes."Why am I doing this? Five years ago, some guy on the internet predicted that Argentina and Spain would be in the World Cup final and that the score would be 3-2. How did this guy know these boys would be in the final? And then they are."Let's go. There it is, McGregor's World Cup final bet. Some guy on the internet, bring it home for me, baby. Let's go."McGregor also shared a screenshot of the betting slip, which showed odds of 36-1. Had Argentina won 3-2 in regulation time, the bet would have returned approximately $3.6 million.The remarkable prediction came close in one aspect, correctly identifying Spain and Argentina as the two finalists five years in advance.The scoreline, however, could not have been further from reality.Rather than producing the anticipated five-goal spectacle, the final developed into a tense tactical contest dominated by Spain's midfield. Article Summary: Conor McGregor lost a $100,000 wager on the FIFA World Cup final. The former UFC two-weight champion backed Argentina to defeat Spain 3-2 in normal time. Article Title: FIFA World Cup 2026: Spain become first world champions to achieve this incredible feat
Article Text:

How Spain's unbeaten run unfolded



Ferran Torres delivers the winning goal



NEW DELHI: Spain's FIFA World Cup 2026 triumph was about much more than lifting the trophy. Luis de la Fuente's side created history by becoming only the fourth team to win a World Cup without trailing for a single minute during the tournament.Before Spain, only Italy (1938), Italy (1982) and Germany (1990) had achieved the feat.La Roja also set another remarkable record. They became the first World Cup-winning team to concede just one goal throughout the entire tournament.Spain sealed their second World Cup title with a 1-0 extra-time win over defending champions Argentina at the New York New Jersey Stadium.Spain began their campaign with a surprise 0-0 draw against World Cup debutants Cabo Verde despite creating 27 chances. They then defeated Saudi Arabia 4-0, with Lamine Yamal scoring his first World Cup goal and becoming Spain's second-youngest scorer.A hard-fought 1-0 victory over Uruguay, courtesy of Alex Baena's goal, helped Spain finish top of their group.In the knockout rounds, Spain beat Austria 3-0, with Mikel Oyarzabal scoring twice and Pedro Porro adding another. Goalkeeper Unai Simon also broke Walter Zenga's World Cup record by going 519 minutes without conceding.Spain then edged Portugal 1-0 after substitute Mikel Merino scored a stoppage-time winner set up by Ferran Torres.In the quarter-finals, Merino struck again as Spain defeated Belgium 2-1 after Fabian Ruiz had opened the scoring.Spain produced one of their best performances in the semi-finals, beating France 2-0 through Oyarzabal's penalty and Pedro Porro's goal.Finally, Torres' extra-time strike against Argentina completed a memorable campaign as Spain lifted the World Cup for the second time while setting two extraordinary records.The decisive moment came in the 106th minute. Argentina were down to 10 men after Enzo Fernandez was sent off in the 93rd minute.Lamine Yamal started the move down the right before finding Pedro Porro. The full-back's cross was about to go out of play, but substitute Nico Williams headed it back into the middle. Another substitute, Ferran Torres, met the ball perfectly with his left foot to beat Emiliano Martínez.It was Spain's 20th shot of the match, while Argentina had still not managed an attempt on goal.After scoring, Torres celebrated by kicking the corner flag before being mobbed by his teammates.Reflecting on his match-winning goal, Torres said: “I think at the end of the day, it was a goal scored by 47 million people,” Torres said. “I feel very happy. I was heavily criticized during the World Cup, but I think it was written in destiny and things. But I always have that chance, that option to continue, and God gives it to those who believe it, who deserve it most.”Torres almost scored again later in extra time but was ruled offside as Spain held on to become world champions.
Article Summary: Spain became only the fourth team to win a World Cup without trailing for a single minute during the tournament. La Roja became the first World Cup-winning team to concede just one goal throughout the entire tournament. Spain sealed their second World Cup title with a 1-0 extra-time win over defending champions Argentina.

The curtain has only just fallen on the 2026 FIFA World Cup , with Spain defeating Argentina 1-0 after extra time in the final to lift their second world title, but preparations for the next edition of football's biggest tournament are already well underway.Much like the 2026 edition, which was hosted by three countries, the United States, Canada and Mexico, all of whom qualified automatically as hosts, the 2030 tournament will also feature multiple host nations receiving direct entry.The 2030 FIFA World Cup will be unlike any previous edition, with six nations already assured of their places and the competition set to span three continents in a historic celebration marking 100 years since the inaugural World Cup.The 2030 tournament will make history as the first FIFA World Cup to be hosted primarily by three countries across two continents.Spain, Portugal and Morocco were selected as the main hosts of the competition, with all three nations receiving automatic qualification as tournament hosts.However, FIFA has also approved a unique centenary celebration that will take the tournament back to where it all began.To commemorate 100 years since the first FIFA World Cup was staged in 1930, the opening three matches of the tournament will be played in South America before the competition moves permanently to Europe and Africa.Those matches will be hosted by Uruguay, Argentina and Paraguay, meaning all three countries have also automatically qualified.That brings the total number of confirmed participants to six before qualifying has even begun.The decision reflects the historical significance of South America in World Cup history.The inaugural FIFA World Cup was held in Uruguay in 1930, with the hosts defeating Argentina in the final to become the first-ever world champions.Montevideo, where that tournament took place, will host the official centenary celebration, recognising Uruguay's unique place in football history.Argentina was selected in recognition of its role as runners-up in the first World Cup, while Paraguay was included because it is home to CONMEBOL, South America's governing body and the only continental football confederation that existed when the inaugural tournament was played.Explaining the decision, FIFA said on its official website: "The 2030 edition is a symbolic milestone for FIFA, as it celebrates 100 years since the first FIFA World Cup was played in South America across three stadiums."Following extensive consultation with all confederations, the FIFA Council approved a unique celebration of the centenary of the FIFA World Cup in South America, specifically in Uruguay, Argentina and Paraguay."FIFA also explained how the hosting proposal came together."The candidacy of Morocco, Portugal and Spain for the FIFA World Cup 2030 was proposed by CAF and UEFA."Similarly, the candidacy of Uruguay, Argentina and Paraguay for the centenary celebration was proposed by CONMEBOL. Those three confederations endorsed the overall proposal of these candidacies."With regard to the latter, subject to the successful bidding process outlined above and approval by the FIFA Congress, the centenary game will be played in Montevideo, Uruguay, as part of the centenary celebration and ceremony, in recognition of Uruguay's role as the hosts and winners of the 1930 edition."A game will be played in Argentina in recognition of Argentina's role as runners-up of the 1930 edition. A game will be played in Paraguay in recognition of Paraguay's role as the home of CONMEBOL, the first confederation and the only one at the time of the 1930 edition."The following nations have already secured their places at the 2030 FIFA World Cup:FIFA's approved hosting plan currently includes 23 proposed stadiums spread across the six host countries.With six nations already confirmed and a centenary celebration set to reconnect the World Cup with its origins in South America before the tournament shifts to Europe and Africa, the 2030 edition is shaping up to become one of the most ambitious and symbolic events in the competition's history.
Article Summary: The 2030 FIFA World Cup will be the first to be hosted primarily by three countries across two continents. Spain, Portugal and Morocco were selected as the main hosts of the competition, with all three nations receiving automatic qualification as tournament hosts. FIFA has also approved a unique centenary celebration that will take the tournament back to where it all began in Uruguay in 1930.

Article Title: Camille Kostek says Taylor Swift looked like a real-life princess in custom Dior at her NYC wedding to Travis Kelce
Article Text:
Camille Kostek Was Starstruck at Taylor Swift's Wedding (Getty Images)

What did Camille Kostek say about Taylor Swift's wedding look and the guest list?

Camille Kostek had a front-row seat to what may be the most talked-about wedding of 2025, and she is still processing it. The Sports Illustrated model, 34, attended Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce 's July 3 ceremony at Madison Square Garden alongside her longtime partner Rob Gronkowski and came away with two things: a vivid memory of Swift in custom Dior, and a complete loss for words the moment Julia Roberts walked into the room. Kostek shared both moments exclusively with PEOPLE at Sports Illustrated's Beyond the Pitch event at Cipriani Wall Street on July 18.Kostek did not hold back when describing Swift's bridal appearance. "She literally was like a real-life princess in her custom Dior," she told PEOPLE. Swift and Kelce, both 36, wore custom Christian Dior Haute Couture pieces by creative director Jonathan Anderson. The ceremony had its own unconventional charm — Adam Sandler officiated, Swift's brother Austin served as her man of honor, and Kelce's older brother Jason was best man. For an event attended by an estimated 1,000 guests, details have stayed remarkably quiet.But the moment that genuinely rattled Kostek had nothing to do with the bride. "Julia Roberts — I absolutely was starstruck. Even thinking about her, I lose my train of thought. She's amazing," she said. Coming from someone who regularly moves through celebrity-heavy rooms, that admission carries weight.Gronkowski, meanwhile, could not stop talking about the dance floor."It was top-notch. Hats off to Taylor and Trav. The dance floor -- that's the one thing -- it was popping. It was popping," the 37-year-old said on Tubi's The Other Football. He also painted a scene outside MSG that night: five blocks of black cars lined up bumper to bumper. "It was the most amount of black cars I've ever seen going into Madison Square Garden," he said.Not surprisingly, the wedding also prompted questions Gronkowski was not quite ready for. Standing at one of the most romantic events of the year with a girlfriend of over a decade, people could not resist asking about a proposal. "It also encourages everyone to ask you when you're doing it right in front of your significant other," he told co-host Jameis Winston. "It's a lot of encouragement." Kostek, for her part, has been candid about her own feelings on the subject. Earlier in May, she admitted on PEOPLE's WAG World series that she sometimes catches herself thinking she is behind where she expected to be at this stage of life.
Article Summary: Camille Kostek attended Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce's wedding. The model said she was starstruck by Julia Roberts. Rob Gronkowski said the dance floor was "top-notch" The wedding was attended by 1,000 guests.

Article Title: "How I felt internally....": Gisele Bündchen broke silence on life with Tom Brady and admitted what changed everything
Article Text:
Gisele Bündchen reflected on how her years in Boston during her marriage to Tom Brady transformed her outlook on life. She said the quieter lifestyle helped her find balance, become more present and focus less on external success. Although the couple divorced in 2022, Bündchen still cherishes the memories they created in Boston, where they raised their children before relocating to Florida in 2020.

Gisele Bündchen says Boston helped her find balance during Tom Brady marriage

Gisele Bündchen still cherishes Boston despite moving on

Life in Boston gave Gisele Bündchen far more than a new address. In a rare reflection on her years with former NFL star Tom Brady, the supermodel opened up about how stepping away from the fast pace of her career helped reshape her outlook on life. Speaking to W Magazine, Bündchen explained that the slower lifestyle she embraced in New England became a turning point, allowing her to focus less on achievements and more on inner peace.Bündchen moved to the Boston area in 2007 after her relationship with Tom Brady became serious. At the time, she was already one of the world's most recognised supermodels, travelling constantly and accepting nearly every opportunity that came her way. Living in New England changed that rhythm.Reflecting on those years, she shared how the quieter surroundings encouraged her to slow down and rethink her priorities."I had moved to Boston and was living a much quieter life," Bündchen recalled. "Earlier in my career, everything was about achievement and saying yes to every opportunity."As the years passed, she realised success meant more than professional accomplishments."Over time, I began to understand the importance of finding balance," she continued. "My spiritual practice helped me become more present and more connected to myself. Instead of focusing on external expectations, I started paying attention to how I felt internally."That shift, she explained, transformed both her career and her personal life."That changed everything—not only my work, but also the way I experienced life."Although Bündchen and Brady divorced in 2022 after 13 years of marriage, she still speaks warmly about the city where they raised their family. The couple welcomed son Benjamin and daughter Vivian during their years in Massachusetts, while Brady's eldest son Jack also became part of their close-knit household.When Brady signed with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2020, the family left Boston after more than a decade. Before moving, Bündchen posted a heartfelt farewell to the city that had become home."What a ride the last decade has been. Boston has been so good to us and will always be in our hearts. We will forever have wonderful memories," she wrote. "Our kids were born and raised there and we have made special friendships to last a lifetime."She also thanked the community that supported Brady throughout his legendary New England Patriots career."I'll miss our friends, the beautiful change of seasons and the rides to the stadium to go cheer for Tom and the Pats," she added. "Thank you to everyone who has been so supportive of my husband and our family throughout all these years. We will miss you."Even so, Bündchen has never hidden her struggle with New England's cold winters. In a previous interview with Vogue, she joked that the climate was never her ideal fit."Why do I live here? It's called love," she said. "I love my husband. My kids were born here in our old apartment on Beacon Street. They're little Bostonians, and they love the weather."
Article Summary: Gisele Bündchen and Tom Brady divorced in 2022 after 13 years of marriage. The couple raised their children in Boston before moving to Florida in 2020. She said the quieter lifestyle helped her find balance, become more present and focus less on external success.

Saquon Barkley’s family was at home when burglars reportedly attempted to break into his luxurious home

Are elite NFL players in danger ahead of the new season in the league?

Article Title: Travis Hunter’s wife finally addresses the viral cheating rumor that has followed her for nearly two years
Article Text:
Travis Hunter’s wife finally addresses the viral cheating rumor that has followed her for nearly two years (Instagram)

Leanna Lenee says the viral story had nothing to do with Travis Hunter

Leanna Lenee has heard the rumors for long enough. Nearly two years after old videos and photos sparked cheating allegations online, the wife of Jacksonville Jaguars rookie Travis Hunter has finally shared her side of the story. In a TikTok video posted in July 2026, Lenee denied the claims and explained why she believes the internet built a false narrative around her past.The controversy first exploded in December 2024, just days after Hunter won the Heisman Trophy. While much of the attention should have stayed on the Colorado star's historic achievement, social media quickly shifted its focus to Lenee. Old content resurfaced, criticism snowballed, and cheating rumors spread across several platforms. Now, she has directly responded.Speaking in a TikTok video, Leanna Lenee made it clear that she never cheated on Travis Hunter and challenged the narrative that has followed her since 2024. "The funniest part about this comment is like I literally never cheated," Lenee said in the TikTok video. She explained that the rumors started after people dug through her past while reacting to criticism she received during Hunter's Heisman Trophy celebration in December 2024.According to Leanna Lenee, an old party photo with another man became the center of the story even though, as she described it, the interaction lasted "maybe max 10 minutes." She claimed the moment had nothing to do with Hunter and happened only because she wanted to make her ex-boyfriend jealous.She also said the timing of the incident matters because she and Hunter were not together then. "I hadn't met him in person at that time, definitely wasn't dating him," Lenee said in the same TikTok video. She added that she never spoke to the man again and accused him of chasing "15 minutes of fame" after the clip resurfaced online.The video she referenced became a major talking point in December 2024. According to Page Six, the footage allegedly showed Lenee dancing with a man while wearing a schoolgirl outfit. Although her face was not visible, the outlet reported that viewers linked the person in the video to Lenee because of a visible thigh tattoo and photos she had previously shared wearing the same outfit.TMZ later reported that the footage was from several years earlier, before Lenee and Travis Hunter began their relationship. While neither outlet confirmed the exact date of the recording, both indicated that the clip predated the couple's romance.In late 2024, as the online backlash intensified, both Travis Hunter and Lenee temporarily deactivated their Instagram accounts. The criticism continued for months, but neither publicly addressed the cheating allegations in detail until now.Despite the constant online attention, the couple's relationship moved forward. Travis Hunter proposed before they married in May 2025, and they welcomed their first child in August 2025.Travis Hunter has rarely commented on the criticism directed at his wife, but he has consistently stood by her amid the public scrutiny. Lenee's latest TikTok marks her clearest response yet, as she firmly rejects the cheating allegations and insists the viral story never reflected what actually happened.
Article Summary: Leanna Lenee says she never cheated on Travis Hunter. In a TikTok video posted in July 2026, Lenee denied the claims and explained why she believes the internet built a false narrative around her past. The controversy first exploded in December 2024, just days after Hunter won the Heisman Trophy.

Article Title: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce face a honeymoon race against time as NFL training camp approaches
Article Text:
Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce honeymoon plans (Getty Images)

What are Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift's honeymoon plans?

Is Travis Kelce ready for the 2026 Chiefs season?

Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift have kept things quiet since their July 3 wedding at Madison Square Garden, but that's about to change in the biggest way possible. The newlyweds are reportedly planning an ambitious around-the-world honeymoon spanning the Caribbean, Europe, Asia, and Australia and they're doing it all before Kelce reports to Kansas City Chiefs training camp in late July. A brief Montana stay and a trip to California for JuJu Smith-Schuster's wedding have been the extent of their post-nuptials so far.The scale of what the couple has in mind is striking. According to a source who spoke to The Sun, Kelce and Swift have been coordinating this for weeks and have already told their inner circle not to expect to hear from them. "Unless there is an emergency, they want to limit outside contact to truly immerse themselves in this once-in-a-lifetime experience," the source said.The list of destinations is genuinely ambitious for a trip squeezed into a matter of weeks. The Caribbean, Europe, Asia, Australia -- it reads less like a honeymoon itinerary and more like a world tour. Which, in a way, makes perfect sense for two people whose schedules have been defined by exactly that.The source added that the trip is about something simpler than the spectacle. "It's a once-in-a-lifetime experience where they can just be themselves, enjoy the time together before going back to work.They are really looking forward to it."The window is tight. The entire honeymoon is timed around Kelce's reporting date for Chiefs camp, so the couple will need to move fast and stay off the radar simultaneously.Kelce came close to walking away from football entirely after last season. He ultimately returned on a new three-year deal, and Patrick Mahomes made clear just how much that decision mattered to the locker room."Obviously, he has the physical gifts to go out there and be that size with that speed and looseness and catch the football," Mahomes told Yahoo Sports. "But I think what makes him who he is -- the leader and the person that he is -- the teammates around him want him to succeed because he's gonna give everything he has for the guys around him."Those words carry extra weight given what Kansas City is heading into. Last season was the first time in over a decade that the Chiefs missed the playoffs, and Mahomes is still rehabbing a torn ACL suffered in December. He is on track for Week 1, but no definitive timeline has been confirmed. Kelce returning healthy and motivated matters more now than it might have during the dynasty years.The honeymoon is the last stretch of calm before all of that begins.
Article Summary: Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift have kept things quiet since their July 3 wedding. The newlyweds are reportedly planning an ambitious around-the-world honeymoon. The honeymoon is timed around Kelce's reporting date for Chiefs camp.

Article Title: CBS NFL reporter Melanie Collins turns heads with a stylish golf course look while enjoying the offseason

The NFL offseason has given Melanie Collins a break from the sidelines, and she is making the most of it. The CBS Sports reporter recently caught fans' attention after sharing a stylish look from a day at Ballyhack Golf Club. Her post was not only about fashion. It also featured one of the closest moments of her golfing journey.Collins revealed she came within inches of her first career hole in one, turning a relaxing day on the course into a memorable one. The combination of a near-perfect shot and a sleek golf outfit quickly made the update a talking point among her followers.The popular NFL reporter Melanie Collins shared the update on Instagram from Ballyhack Golf Club, a private course in Virginia. She stepped onto the fairway in a coordinated black golf outfit that included a sleeveless cropped zip-up polo, a matching athletic skort, a black visor and black Nike golf shoes. The clean all-black look stood out as much as her game and drew plenty of attention from fans in the comments.The stylish outfit was not the only thing she spoke about. In the caption, Collins revealed she came heartbreakingly close to her first career hole-in-one. She wrote on Instagram, "This close to my first hole-in-one but hit the base of the pin and lipped out." While she did not share the shot itself, the update showed just how close she came to achieving one of golf's rarest milestonesGolf has become one of Collins' favourite offseason activities, offering a break from the busy NFL calendar before another season begins. Away from football, she often shares moments from the course, travels and outdoor adventures with her followers.Collins has worked as a CBS Sports NFL sideline reporter since joining the network in 2018. She regularly teams up with veteran play-by-play commentator Kevin Harlan and analyst Trent Green during NFL broadcasts. Before CBS, she built her broadcasting resume with Yahoo Sports and ESPN, covering events including the Super Bowl, FIFA World Cup, Winter Olympics and NBA coverage. She also studied sports journalism at Penn State University before beginning her television career.Collins has also become one of the most recognisable sideline reporters in the NFL because of her calm presence during live broadcasts and her ability to deliver updates under pressure. After completing her eighth season with CBS earlier this year, she thanked her colleagues and viewers on Instagram, calling herself grateful for another memorable year covering the league. This offseason has simply offered a different side of her routineWith the NFL season still weeks away, Collins appears to be enjoying every bit of her downtime. Her latest golf outing showed both her growing love for the sport and a polished sense of style, while the near hole-in-one gave fans another reason to follow along before she returns to the NFL sidelines this fall.

Article Title: "It’s almost impossible": Dallas Cowboys Cheerleader Emily Awbrey exposes the hidden struggle behind covering her tattoo
Article Text:
Dallas Cowboys Cheerleader Emily Awbrey explains how she covers her hand tattoo

Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders appearance rules remain unchanged

Making the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders squad takes far more than dance talent. Every detail matters, including appearance. Just days after earning a coveted spot on the 2026-27 roster, rookie Emily Awbrey pulled back the curtain on one of the beauty routines fans had been curious about for months, showing exactly how she hides her hand tattoo to meet the team's long-standing appearance standards.Emily Awbrey's journey to the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders has already become one of the most inspiring stories of the season. After falling short during last year's auditions, she returned determined to earn a place on the iconic squad and successfully secured a spot as one of the team's "comeback girls."Following the announcement, fans who watched America's Sweethearts: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders began asking the same question. How does she cover the hand tattoo that appeared during the Netflix series?Awbrey answered that curiosity herself in a detailed Instagram video, taking followers through every step of the process."I’ve gotten a lot of questions asking how I do it, so I thought I’d do a little video and show you how I cover it," she said.She admitted the process starts with an imperfect canvas because of a recent spray tan."I take this most disgusting, dusty, gross beauty blender that I only use for this," she joked before applying Dermablend leg and body makeup.Rather than piling on a thick coat immediately, Awbrey prefers building coverage gradually."Not a super heavy layer, because we’re going to double layer it," she explained, noting that blending makeup across the entire hand creates a more natural finish. She also works product into every crease by moving her fingers before locking everything in with loose setting powder.The rookie also shared one surprising confession.She told fans "a little secret," revealing that she does not always cover the tattoo on one finger because it is usually hidden by the team's pom-poms.Still, she admitted that concealing tattoos on hands is one of the hardest beauty challenges."It’s almost impossible" because her hands constantly move and rub together, making makeup difficult to keep in place.Awbrey's tutorial also highlighted the strict grooming standards that continue to define the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders.According to the team's official guidelines, hopefuls may audition with tattoos, but no tattoo, regardless of size, can be visible while wearing the uniform or rehearsal attire. That rule has remained in place for decades alongside other appearance expectations covering hair, makeup and overall presentation.To improve the coverage, Awbrey applied another layer of foundation, additional powder and a darker shade that better matched her arm."I don’t think anyone knew I had a hand tattoo until the show came out," she said while demonstrating the final steps.She also warned that patience is essential during the routine."You’ve got to be careful because the more you touch, the more you pick up the foundation, because there’s just a lot of layer there … you can’t blend it too much, you kind of just have to let it low-key sit."After adding bronzer to balance the color from her spray tan, she finished everything with two setting sprays, calling the final step the key to keeping the makeup in place throughout practices and performances.Even then, Awbrey acknowledged the process is not flawless."Is it perfect? No. But it will get the job done, I’d say," she said.Her candid tutorial gave fans a rare behind the scenes look at the preparation required to meet one of professional cheerleading's most recognizable standards, proving that making the squad involves plenty of dedication long before stepping onto the field.
Article Summary: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleader Emily Awbrey explains how she hides her hand tattoo. The team's appearance rules remain unchanged and no tattoo, regardless of size, can be visible while wearing the uniform or rehearsal attire. Her tutorial also highlighted the strict grooming standards that continue to define the team.
